intent: Add a Hebrew public application for individual researchers or institution representatives under owner-published exact conditions. Submission grants no identity or access; private owner review binds a live selected personal code to a study and explicit permissions, atomically imports a draft, and partner folders show each partner's actual current grants across authorized studies. Preserve existing owner authentication, personal-code/current-credential checks, RLS, revocation, consent, released-document rules and immutable signatures; no production, email, paid service, or provider activation.

triage_groups.title: Owner review actions
triage_groups.context: Apply-queue: the owner review screen uses an incomplete study list, cached revisions and an unsavable repeated review action.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Supply the full study list (#1), refresh the selected study revision (#2), and permit another CAS-protected under_review note (#5); preserve exact owner-selected grants.
triage_groups.why: These distinct fixes make the documented owner review path usable across existing studies and repeated reviews.

triage_groups.title: Public submission deadlines
triage_groups.context: Apply-queue: separate browser and access-store waits can keep one public submission pending indefinitely.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Bound the server access-store wait (#8) and browser request lifetime (#3), preserving the same request ID for ambiguous retries.
triage_groups.why: Both boundaries must settle so an applicant can retry without discarding an uncertain submission.

triage_groups.title: Refresh and navigation state
triage_groups.context: Apply-queue: delayed responses can restore old form state or replace a newer owner view.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Read live public controls immediately before any rebuild (#4) and guard owner renders with the current view sequence (#6).
triage_groups.why: The most recent user edit and navigation should survive slower requests.

testing_gaps.title: Test focus and page restoration event refresh
testing_gaps.why_it_matters: A visitor returning to an open, acknowledged form may keep seeing old terms if the new focus or page-restoration listeners stop working. The tests prove that calling load directly clears acknowledgement after a version change, but would still pass if those browser listeners were removed. An event-driven browser test would verify that the refresh actually occurs when the visitor returns.
